rv.q: "Gaslight" is very much my favorite of all Northlight's recent holiday shows...

Jessica Thebus’ production of a husband subtly trying to drive his wealthy wife crazy, in order to steal from her, is the basis for this Victorian mystery.
It’s stylishly creepy, surprisingly funny and triumphantly feminist.
All in all, “Gaslight” is a fabulous experience to witness at this holiday season.
Subtle menace underscores director Jessica Thebus’ taut, expertly acted production that’s carefully staged to balance tension and humor, including some stage business that borders on farcical.
Director Jessica Thebus , clearly in command, puts the cast through their paces with an energy more suited to screwball comedy than thriller.
If you enjoy a good mystery, you will adore this one.

cn.t: Critics praise this gripping production of "Gaslight" as a taut, thrilling adaptation that remains compelling even when the twist is known, with standout performances and atmospheric design that brilliantly captures Victorian psychological manipulation.
